title: White City Ballroom; Louis, Bix and the gang's after-hours nights
summary: At White City Ballroom the band swings, Louis listens, and everyone goes to the Sunset Cafe and then to Jimmie Noone at the Onyx.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: It was something. Everybody was talking about us. Louis Armstrong used to come over and sit behind the bandstand before he went to work at Sunset Café. Two or three nights a week. You know, sometimes a couple of times a week he'd come over and just sit and listen to us play. We were really (out of) it you know. Louis would come over and hear us, but the band was swinging and it was a good band.

Bix Beiderbecke and Frankie (Trumbauer Pee Wee (Trombone?), Peter Russell and those guys came up from Hudson Lake, Indiana on their night off, Monday nights. And they'd come up and listen to us that night. And we'd finish at twelve o'clock and then we'd all go to hear Louis Armstrong at the Sunset Café.

En Mass, en masse, everybody would go. We would sit in with Louis and then we'd go across the street to the Onyx Club, Jimmy Noon, he was the clarinet player. He was one of our great jazz men. And then we'd all sit in up there with Jimmy Noon until three, four five o'clock in the morning we'd get out of there, six o'clock sometimes.
Bix Beiderbecke and (Trumbauer (Trombone?) and Benny Goodman Tough Davey (Tessmacher (Tessmacher)), all the guys. Bud Freeman
And that's where we, I guess that started the integration musically style xxxxxxxx you know.
